title: Adaptive stride sampling and trace linkage for inference metrics pipeline
text:
Adaptive stride sampling and trace linkage for inference metrics pipeline

description:
Problem: Our current metrics ingestion pipeline for inference traffic is producing very high-cardinality labels and uneven sampling across models and sequence lengths, leading to excessive storage costs and noisy SLOs. In particular, tail latency exemplars are not consistently linked to traces when requests are routed through async queues and cross-service proxies, making posthoc root-cause analysis slow.

Goal: Implement an adaptive 'stride' sampling mechanism in the ingest sidecar plus deterministic trace linkage for Prometheus exemplars and OTel spans that: (1) reduces metric cardinality without biasing latency SLOs, (2) preserves representative tail examples and links them to traces, and (3) is compatible with existing Prometheus histogram+exemplar pipelines and our OTLP relay.

Scope:
- Sidecar sampling component that uses a stride window per (model, route, region, quantization_profile) to forward 1/N of counters/histogram exemplars and always forward a configurable fraction of suspected high-latency requests.
- Deterministic sampling seed derived from request attributes to ensure reproducibility across retries/buffered queues.
- Trace ID propagation and exemplar->trace mapping: ensure exemplar labels include trace_id and span_id (where policy allows), and for private deployments provide an opt-in hashing mode to avoid plaintext PII in metrics.
- OTLP->Prometheus adaptor changes to preserve exemplar trace linkage and attach trace context when scraping or converting histograms.
- Dashboard and alert updates: provide SLO-corrected extrapolation metrics and an 'exemplar explorer' panel that jumps to the linked trace in the trace UI.

acceptance_criteria:
Stride sidecar deployed on canary hosts that reduces ingestion volume by >=40% for sampled workloads without increasing SLO breach rate on existing alerts (validated vs baseline)
Exemplars emitted for p99 tail requests include trace_id (or hashed trace_id in private mode) and link to trace viewer; tests verify round-trip trace lookup for 95% of exemplars
Deterministic sampling ensures stable sampling rate across retries and queued replays (unit tests + e2e replay tests)
Prometheus histogram ingestion preserves exemplar->trace mapping when converted from OTLP; existing dashboards updated and smoke-tested
Documentation and runbook updated: config knobs, privacy modes, and rollback steps

comments:
2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: kickoff sync held with Observability, Runtime, and Routing teams. Agree to implement stride sidecar and a small OTLP adapter change. Action: Marco to prototype stride window and tabletop sampling algorithm.
2026-02-28 - Marco Alvarez: prototype complete. Using a circular stride counter keyed by (model, route, profile) stored in memory with optional shared backend (Redis) for Dedicated clusters. Prototype reduces cardinality by ~48% in traffic replay. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1723
2026-03-03 - Design review (observability): discussed privacy mode for traces. Decision: support two modes - 'trace_id' (default) and 'trace_hash' (sha256 hex truncated) for Private deployments. Added feature flag and config at sidecar level.
2026-03-06 - QA: integration tests flaked on async queue replay; root cause was non-deterministic request IDs. Action: add deterministic seed derivation from request.start_time + routed_shard_id
2026-03-10 - Marco Alvarez: OTLP->Prometheus adaptor updated to copy trace context into exemplar metadata and to annotate histogram buckets with exemplar refs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1779
2026-03-12 - Observability lead (Janet Liu): canary rollout started on 3 hosts in us-west; monitoring ingestion volume and SLO alerts. No regressions observed in first 24h. Next: expand to 20 hosts and run full traffic replay test on staging.
